Cautiously optimistic with measured tightening, but the July SLOOS points to mild credit headwinds that temper the outlook.

- FOMC stance: Labor market solid and growth moderate; inflation below 2% with symmetric target; policy on hold with balance sheet normalization beginning—gradualism and accommodative bias remain.
- SLOOS cross-check: Banks reported weaker demand in several credit segments (CRE, construction/land development/multifamily; consumer auto and credit cards), with demand roughly unchanged for some nonfarm nonresidential loans. Standards eased for residential mortgages (including jumbo/QM/GSE) but tightened for consumer loans (auto and credit cards). Foreign banks tightened standards across C&I (small, middle-market, large) and CRE, even as some saw stronger CRE demand.
- Implication: Softer loan demand and tighter standards in cyclical/consumer categories, alongside foreign-bank tightening, suggest a modest drag on investment and consumption. This credit-channel signal reinforces the Fed’s cautious, data-dependent path, especially with inflation still below target.

Net: Still slightly positive given labor strength and ongoing accommodation, but SLOOS dynamics warrant a notch more caution than before.
